title: EPOC: An Efficient Pulse Generation Framework with Advanced Synthesis for Quantum Circuits
problem: Quantum optimal control has high computational overhead and generates long circuit latencies; gate-based pulse generation requires substantial resource overhead.
motivation: Reducing pulse generation computational cost and circuit latency is critical for practical quantum circuit execution on near-term quantum devices.
method: EPOC uses ZX-Calculus, a mathematical form that reveals equivalent ways to arrange a quantum circuit, to explore more parallelizable circuit organizations. The framework breaks pulse generation into smaller, more controllable units (finer granularity) and partitions the circuit into independent segments that can process in parallel. Synthesis techniques then optimize these segments into efficient pulse instructions, reducing both the computational cost of pulse generation and circuit execution time.
key_novelty: EPOC is the first to combine ZX-Calculus circuit representation, circuit partitioning, and synthesis techniques to generate quantum pulses with reduced computational overhead and increased parallelism.
contributions: Novel combination of ZX-Calculus and circuit partitioning for pulse generation
Finer-granularity pulse generation enabling increased parallelism
